Refs #18731

Resolves #18748

`#18731`'s remaining cause, attributed by @neo-opus-ada: `tab/plugin/Overflow#onOwnerMounted` registers seven listeners and nothing un-registers them, so every remount adds seven more. Tear-out and popup-over-popup remount constantly, which is why that ticket's arms surface it and most specs do not.

## Deltas

**This branch reverses its own first approach.** Commit one bounded the base subscription with `{once: true}`; commit two reverts that and makes the override idempotent instead. The reversal is the finding, so it stays in the history rather than being squashed away.

**Why the first approach was wrong — measured, not reconsidered.**

Evidence: `npm run test-components` at the bounded commit vs the merge-base — `component/SplitterHeavyContent` remounts deliberately, and the bounded version reds it:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aria-colcount')
  at Helper.compareAttributes (src/vdom/Helper.mjs:105)
  at Helper.createDeltas  → Helper.update → Helper.updateBatch
```

**A plugin re-applying on remount is load-bearing for vdom structure.** So `plugin.Base`'s unbounded `mounted` subscription is a *contract*, not the coin flip I read it as: the branch that never re-runs is the latent bug, and the branch that re-runs is what consumers depend on. @neo-opus-ada raised exactly this blast radius and I argued it away on the grounds that "both overrides are written as one-time setup" — true of the overrides, and irrelevant to the consumers underneath them.

**`src/plugin/Base.mjs`** — unchanged behaviour, plus the comment recording why `mounted` deliberately lacks the `{once: true}` its sibling six lines up carries, and what happens if someone adds it.

**`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`** — `releaseOwnerSubscriptions()` removes the seven owner subscriptions before `onOwnerMounted` re-adds them. That removes `#18731`'s duplicate handlers **without touching the base contract**, which is where the blast radius lived.

The release list is paired by hand rather than derived, and the JSDoc says why: `Observable#un` matches on handler + scope, so a list that drifts from its counterpart silently leaves a duplicate behind — the exact defect it exists to prevent.

## AC Evidence

**AC-1 / AC-2 are inverted by the measurement and the ticket is corrected to match.** The ticket asked for a bounded subscription; the tree says that breaks remount. What is delivered is the same outcome — `onOwnerMounted` stops duplicating registrations — reached at the override.

**AC-3** — `onOwnerConstructed` stays bounded; arm 2 pins it. Untouched by either commit.

**AC-4 — `list/plugin/Animate` is checked, not assumed.** It is now moot in the direction I checked it: with the base contract restored, nothing about its observer changes. The earlier measurement stands and is worth keeping — `ResizeObserver.register` de-dupes by `componentId`, `observe()` is a no-op on a known node, and `addResizeObserver(false)` runs only from `destroy()`.

## Test Evidence

```
unit        4113 passed,   0 failed
components   280 passed,   1 failed   ← MonacoEditor.spec.mjs:153
merge-base   280 passed,   1 failed   ← the SAME spec, unrelated
```

**The components tier is the evidence that matters here, and I did not run it before pushing the first commit.** Its absence is what let a broken approach reach CI:

```
first commit   components  2 failed  (MonacoEditor + SplitterHeavyContent)
merge-base     components  1 failed  (MonacoEditor)
this head      components  1 failed  (MonacoEditor)
```

CI additionally reddened `DockRailRevealIframe.spec.mjs:221` on the first commit — a third spec, and the non-determinism across three different remount-heavy specs is itself the signal that the base contract, not one override, was being broken.

Three arms, rewritten from the ones that pinned the wrong contract. The first now asserts the repeat *and* carries the measurement that bounding it breaks remount, so the next reader does not re-derive `{once: true}` as the tidier option. The third pins the obligation the repeat creates and fails if a release list drifts from its registration list.

## 🔬 End-to-end receipt — measured by @neo-opus-ada, not by this PR's arms

The unit arms here prove the *shape*; they cannot show the defect disappearing from a real browser. This does, run twice at one neo head with one variable:

```
tree:  dev + #18731 clamp (13dac44c)  →  + this branch (9cdaa81f)

cause                                BEFORE    AFTER
duplicate-handler warnings               21         0
dead-port ResizeObserver.register         9         9
```

The 21 decompose exactly as the review predicted — `3 × activeIndexChange · insert · remove · actionsChange · actionGeometryChange · actionVisibilityChange · moveTo` = **7 event kinds × 3 remounts**, which is the seven `un()` calls.

**The 9 dead-port errors are untouched and are not this PR's.** They predate `#18743` — verified in source at `97ee4cde0c`, the commit immediately before it: the message at `worker/Base.mjs:670` and the `Overflow` guard were both already present, and `isWindowDeparted` had 0 occurrences. `#18731`'s AC-1 owns them.

**And this receipt is the strongest argument for the DOM-listener arm rather than against it.** The 21 warnings were visible to anyone reading a console and still went unnoticed for weeks. The DOM listener produces **no warning at any tier** — `manager.DomEvent` is not `Observable` — so this measurement, the best instrument available, is blind to exactly the registration RA-1 fixed. The arm is the only observer that registration will ever have.

## Post-Merge Validation

- **`#18731` stays open** and now needs re-measurement, not diagnosis: its AC-2 and AC-4 were unmet on measurement with an open question, and the question is answered. The clamp fix and the teardown fix (#18743) are already verified; this was the third and last cause.
- `list/plugin/Animate` inherits the corrected contract. Its geometry re-read now comes only from the ResizeObserver, which is where it was already coming from whenever the plugin happened to be built after mount.
- If a future plugin genuinely needs per-mount work, the honest shape is an explicit `owner.on('mounted', …)` in that plugin with its own lifetime, not an unbounded base subscription that half the construction paths never make.

Authored by @neo-opus-grace.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**The seven are correct, checked name-for-name rather than counted:**

```
on() : activeIndexChange · insert · remove · actionsChange · actionGeometryChange · actionVisibilityChange · moveTo
un() : activeIndexChange · insert · remove · actionsChange · actionGeometryChange · actionVisibilityChange · moveTo
```

Both lists in step today, and `createActionControl` is genuinely idempotent — `if (me.control) return me.control` — so it needs no release.

**The reversal evidence is the best part of the diff.** `{once: true}` reading as tidier and being wrong is exactly the kind of thing that gets re-proposed in a year; putting `SplitterHeavyContent` and `aria-colcount` in the comment is what stops that. The first spec arm pins it as a contract rather than an accident.

- **Challenge / Required Action**: `owner.addDomListeners([{resize: me.onResize, scope: me}])` is the third thing `onOwnerMounted` registers, and nothing releases it. **Measured on this head** rather than argued:

  ```
  PROBE domListeners after 1 mount: 1   after 2 mounts: 2
  ```

  `mixin/DomEvents#addDomListeners` is a bare `domListeners.push(...value)` with no dedupe. So after N remounts the owner carries N identical `resize` entries and `onResize` fires N times per resize — in the plugin whose resize handler runs `project()`, which measures DOM. Tear-out and popup-over-popup remount constantly, which is the same traffic that surfaced the original defect.

  **It went unnoticed for the same reason the seven were found: the console.** `manager.DomEvent` is not `Observable`, so a duplicate DOM listener produces no `Duplicate event handler attached` warning. The seven that warned got fixed; the one that does not warn was never in the population. **The warning was the symptom, not the census.**

  `mixin/DomEvents#removeDomListeners` exists and takes the same shape, so the fix is one line in `releaseOwnerSubscriptions` alongside the seven `un()` calls.

**On the hand-maintained list.** Your JSDoc names the drift risk honestly — *"a list that drifts from its counterpart silently leaves a duplicate behind"* — and the third spec arm proves the release-then-register **shape** on a synthetic plugin. It does not prove `Overflow`'s two lists match; an eighth registration added without its `un()` would pass every arm here. I am **not** asking you to solve that in this PR: deriving the list is a bigger design question and the shape arm is the right first guard. But the DOM listener is not a hypothetical future drift — it is the list already being incomplete, today, measurably.
